text.text_excerpt: This is one of the best bars/restaurants in the area. I know there are at least four separate bars there but they each have their own old school classic look and feel. There is an awesome relaxing courtyard with a fountain in the middle of it and a convenient outdoor bar. The poor staff have to wear green ensembles but I think it really does improve the customers experience. We were there amidst the unfortunate polar vortex so the patio wasn't too crowded. We were able to relax and and enjoy a couple hurricanes before our scandalous cocktail tour took off. I don't ordinarily like drinking sweet alcohol but my hurricane was simply scrumptious. YUM. I think I could have had four. I will def...

Ms. Patricia served us drinks and she was amazing. She's been working there 50 years and we can't suggest that you go see her strongly enough. The hurricanes and cyclones are delicious. I love the souvenir glasses, they are a nice treat and the piano bar was fun. We had a nice jam session with music from Bobby Brown, Salt and Pepa and yes even Tupac. This place is a must stop no matter now crowded they have 5 bars so you'll get a drink in no time. The courtyard is very nice. There's a fountain and on a nice day it's the ideal place to have drinks. We didn't have lunch so I'm excited to go back to try the food. I've been making drinks at home for years using the Pat O'briens mix so this wa...

Pat O'Brien's is an institution. You owe it to yourself to come here and have a hurricane during your stay in New Orleans. With that said, I don't like, actually I loathe, hurricanes and long since checked that syrupy concoction off my bucket list and moved on. Despite my hatred for hurricanes, Pat O's is still one of my favorite bars in the Quarter. This past trip we wound up accidentally spending a few hours here thanks to torrential downpours. Trust me, it's not a bad place to get stuck. Even with the infamous 21+ courtyard patio rained out, this place was hopping. The piano bar is also a ton of fun.
